newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shanghai Ind shares rise on warrant talk.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Ind shares rise on warrant talk.

text.p: Shares of Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd rose on Wednesday on talk of a covered warrant issue on the stock, brokers said.

"The issue size of the warrants is expected to be 84.9 million warrants," said one dealing manager at a regional brokerage. Traders said gearing ratio was expected to be four times with a premium of 24.98 percent.
The shares were up HK$0.80 at HK$25.50 in late trade after hitting an all time high of HK$25.55 per share.
Volume was 7.13 million shares worth HK$179.53 million.
Talk of warrant issues often lift shares on the expectation the issuer will buy stock to cover its position.
Analysts also said the company's recently announced asset injections would result in a higher net asset value, boosting demand for the Shanghai-concept stock.

The company, a locally incorporated company controlled by the Shanghai municipal government, had said earlier the HK$2.7 billion asset injections into the company would lift the proportion of its Shanghai investment to 56 percent of the company's total investment from a current 10 percent.
